chunks: All that he claims will revert to Us, and he will come before Us all alone.

key_terms.وَنَرِثُهُ: And We inherit him / We take possession of what he claims
key_terms.وَيَأْتِينَا: And he will come to Us

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when God says 'he will come before Us all alone' in Surah Maryam?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the finality of individual accountability, where one's own words and deeds become the sole 'inheritance' or legacy presented before Allah, stripping away social status or intercessors. It highlights the transition from communal life to absolute solitude, emphasizing that the self is both the witness and the accused. This reinforces the concept of *Hisab* (accountability) where external validations vanish, leaving only the truth of one's assertions.
